text:
Matias Maccelli's Islanders season came in two parts: a hot start, then a lower-body injury in Toronto on Oct. 17 that cost him almost a month. Since coming back on Nov. 12 he has four assists in four games, and he's at 10 points in 12 games overall.

The role is the story. He's on the ice for 78% of the Islanders' power-play chances, up from 31% last season in Toronto, and that's driving a breakout flag in our numbers: 0.83 points a game against 0.55 last season. Twelve games is a small sample, but ice time settles faster than scoring does, and the role looks real.

Some of the scoring will cool. New York has scored 5 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, so the assists are getting help. His passing is no fluke, though. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 20% of his setups crossing the royal road, nearly three times a typical forward's rate, and put him in the 92nd percentile for primary shot assists. On a power play with Mathew Barzal back, that skill has a lot to work with.
headline: Maccelli found a power-play home on Long Island
